Kodely generates a real, unique React site and publishes it free to a live kodely.site URL — no generic template grid.", "targetKeyword": "build a link-in-bio page with AI", "category": "Use-Cases", "bodyHtml": "

What a good link-in-bio page actually needs

A link-in-bio page has one job: take the single link your social profile allows and turn it into several. Done well, it needs surprisingly little. A clear sense of who you are in the first five seconds. A short, prioritized list of the links that actually matter — your shop, your latest video, your booking page, not fifteen buttons competing for attention. And a look that feels like you, not like a template a few million other creators are also using.

That third point is where most link-in-bio tools quietly fall short. They solve identity and link organization fine. Distinct design is the part they were never built for.

The honest tradeoff: Kodely vs. dedicated link-in-bio tools

Tools like Linktree and Beacons exist specifically for this job, and they do one thing better than Kodely: click analytics. If you need to see which link got tapped, which day drove traffic, or you are judging a campaign by click-through numbers, those platforms have tracking built in. Kodely does not have analytics tracking today. That is a real limitation, and worth knowing before you commit an hour to building something.

What you get in exchange is a page that is not visibly built on a template. Most link-in-bio pages share the same stacked-button layout, the same rounded pill shapes, the same recognizable shell — because thousands of accounts run the identical underlying template with different colors dropped in. A page built with Kodely is a real, independent site: your layout, your typography, your structure, generated from how you described it rather than poured into someone else's grid. Visitors see a page, not a Linktree.

If click tracking is non-negotiable for you, use a dedicated tool. If you want a bio page that looks unmistakably like yours, that is what one prompt gets you here.

The one-prompt approach

Instead of picking a template and swapping colors, you describe the page you want in plain English, the way you would brief a designer. Who you are, what you want visitors to click first, and the mood — minimal, bold, playful, whatever fits. Kodely turns that description into an actual coded site in one pass, then you refine it from there.

An example prompt

Here is a realistic prompt for a fitness coach launching a bio page:

Build a link-in-bio page for me, a strength coach named Dana Reyes. Dark background, one bold accent color in warm orange, big confident headline with my name and the tagline ‘Strength coaching, no fluff.’ Below that, five link buttons in this order: Book a free consult, Instagram, my YouTube channel, my training program (Gumroad), and email me. Keep it tight on mobile, no clutter, and give it a slightly editorial feel rather than a typical app-style layout.

Kodely reads that and generates a working page matching the layout, tone, and priority order you specified — not a generic five-button stack with your name pasted on top.

What Kodely actually generates

This is not a mockup or a flat HTML page. Kodely builds a real Vite + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS v4 application, starting from a real foundation codebase with hand-built UI primitives. Your link-in-bio page is made of actual component files, and the live preview you see while it builds is the real compiled app rendering, not a static image. If you want to see the code, the in-app code view shows the actual generated source files so you can inspect or copy them. There is no zip export yet — viewing and copying in-app is how you get at the code today.

Customizing your page in chat

Once the first version exists, changes work the same way: describe them. Move the booking link to the top, swap the accent color, add a sixth link for a new drop — Kodely edits the real components behind the page rather than regenerating from scratch. Every successful generation is saved as a checkpoint, so if a change goes sideways, rolling back to the previous version is free and instant.

Publishing to a live URL

When the page looks right, one click publishes it to a real public address at yourname.kodely.site. It is free and included — there is no separate hosting step, no extra checkout, no hosting bill to think about. Every publish is automatically scanned for accidentally leaked secrets or API keys before it goes live, so you are not shipping something you will regret.

FAQ

Does Kodely track clicks on my links?

No. Kodely does not have built-in analytics today. If click tracking is essential, pair your page with a link-shortening or analytics tool, or use a dedicated link-in-bio product instead.

Can I use my own domain, like danareyes.com?

Not yet. Published pages live at a *.kodely.site subdomain only.

Can I download the code and host it myself?

Not yet — there is no zip export. You can view and copy the generated source files from the in-app code view.

Do I need to know how to code?

No. You describe the page in chat and Kodely writes the real React components for you.

What does it cost?

New accounts get 750 credits free, no credit card required, and a build that fails to compile is never charged. Beyond the free credits, top-ups are $9 for 500 credits, $40 for 2,500 credits (most popular), and $90 for 6,000 credits — credits never expire. See /pricing for details.

Build your link-in-bio page free and see your own design, not a template, live at your own kodely.site address in minutes.
